gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the cheapest in-stock setup sized for 3 days at 1 kWh/day is BLUETTI's Apex 200 + B300K: 5,324.8 Wh for $2,199 at bluettipower.com on 2026-11-17. That is $0.41/Wh, about 4.5 freezer-days at ChatGPT's own 85% assumption. It also has 30% more capacity than the $3,099 DELTA Pro 3 ChatGPT picked, and both other ChatGPT picks (the Anker F3800/F3800 Plus and the Jackery 5000 Plus) are sold out at their makers' US stores.
standout_why: I compared against the cited pages. us.ecoflow.com's DELTA Pro 3 page is the only cited product page and would not load (HTTP 429). ankersolix.com's F3800 and F3800 Plus pages show 'Price Loading' and 'Sold Out'. solarwaypoint.com's F3800 vs DELTA Pro 3 vs Jackery 5000 Plus comparison gives no price, $/Wh, idle draw or freezer runtime and lists no other models. None of these pages prices the category or names any station outside those three. ChatGPT's answer also had no sub-$2,500 option and showed the Jackery as available at $4,639.
decides: It changes the pick on value. At ChatGPT's 1 kWh/day freezer and 85% usable energy, Apex 200 + B300K gives 5,324.8 × 0.85 ÷ 1,000 ≈ 4.5 days for $2,199. DELTA Pro 3 (4,096 Wh) gives about 3.5 days at ChatGPT's $3,099, or at the $2,799 our page read on 2026-11-03. The bundle also takes up to 3,000 W of solar (2,000 W of that on the 60–280 V MC4 input), so the 'does solar help' half is covered too. The cheaper single units each miss 72 h at 1 kWh/day: Elite 300 gets about 2.6 days at $1,199, Apex 200 alone about 2.2 days at $1,099, and EcoFlow says the DELTA 3800 Gen4 at $1,699 'powers a refrigerator for up to 70 hours'. They only make 3 days with an efficient 0.6 kWh/day freezer or with solar help.
